Subject: Downstream vendor addition — Durable Analytics (onward transfer permission)

Hi Vivek,

Quick note from MedOps' security and procurement teams — we're planning to onboard Durable Analytics, Inc. for log analytics and long-term retention of de-identified telemetry from our Redwood-hosted inference workloads. Because Durable will receive logs that originate from Redwood's processing of our customer data, procurement flagged this as an "onward transfer" under the DPA and asked us to get explicit permission and subprocessor details from Redwood.

Could you please provide: 
- Redwood's current subprocessor roster and confirmation that Durable is an approved downstream recipient, or the process/timeline to evaluate and approve them;
- Any SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ evidence packets you can share (or a pointer to the security portal);
- Confirmation of SCCs applicability and whether PHI/PII categories change the approval path (MedOps handles limited PHI in logs — we're attaching a short inventory).

Attaching: medops_vendor_inventory_20270301.xlsx (shows the proposed data fields and retention needs).

We'd like to complete this before the end of next week to stay on our rollout schedule. Who should I expect to coordinate with on Redwood's side for the review?

Thanks,
Katherine Lopez
Sr. Security Program Manager
MedOps Health

Katherine —

Thanks for the heads up and for attaching the inventory. I've looped in Monica on Security and Aditya on Legal/Contracts so we can route the request through our DPA/onward-transfer review. High-level answers up front: Redwood maintains a published subprocessor roster and a security evidence portal; we evaluate downstream recipients for data classification, SCCs, and any HIPAA applicability. If MedOps is sending PHI into logs, that will change the approval path and require additional attestation.

Next steps I propose:
- Monica, can you confirm what packet we can share (SOC 2 report redacted summary, SIG questionnaire response, and the CAIQ snapshot)?
- Aditya, can Legal confirm whether Durable Analytics would be treated as an "onward transferee" under our DPA and what gating language we need?
- Katherine, can you confirm whether the logs will include any PHI identifiers (e.g., MRN, patient name) or only pseudonymized/session IDs? If it's only pseudonymized telemetry, list the exact fields you plan to send.

I'll keep this thread for audit trail.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Vivek / Katherine —

Thanks for the context. For MedOps' review I've attached our current subprocessor roster PDF and a filled dataflow matrix that maps fields -> purpose -> retention -> encryption at rest/in transit. In short:

- Redwood will treat Durable Analytics as a downstream data processor and will require a written permissive acknowledgement from MedOps before authorizing transfer.
- We can share a redacted SOC 2 summary and CAIQ snapshot via the security portal link below; full SOC 2 report requires an NDA.
- SCCs are applicable for EU-origin data; if MedOps' logs include EU residents we will need executed SCCs between Redwood and MedOps and an additional flow-down requirement to Durable.
- HIPAA: if you are sending any 18 HIPAA identifiers, we will need an executed BAA between MedOps and Redwood and flow-down controls to Durable (we treat PHI as higher risk and require quarterly security attestations).

Action items for MedOps to confirm:
1) Exact list of fields being forwarded (please highlight if any of those are PHI).
2) Retention window you need for Durable (we will only allow retention aligned to the DPA unless there's a documented business need).
3) Whether Durable will have ability to re-identify or export data outside the contract boundaries.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_202702.pdf; dataflow_matrix_medops_durableanalytics.pdf

Security portal: https://security.redwood.example/evidence/portal (CAIQ & SOC 2 redacted packet)

Monica Patel
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Katherine / MedOps procurement team —

Thanks for the patience while we completed our internal review. Based on the materials provided and Redwood's risk assessment, Redwood is prepared to authorize the onward transfer to Durable Analytics subject to the following conditions:

1) MedOps signs and returns the enclosed permission acknowledgement (we've attached a Docusign link and an unsigned PDF for record).
2) Durable Analytics must accept flow-down obligations: SCCs for EU data, encryption-at-rest and in-transit requirements, and a 90-day breach notification SLA.
3) If MedOps confirms any of the fields are PHI, MedOps and Redwood must execute a BAA before transfer.
4) Retention at Durable is capped at the window listed in the submitted inventory unless Redwood and MedOps agree in writing to a longer retention.

We will not permit Durable to re-distribute the data to third-party resellers without separate written approval. Once the signed permission is returned, Redwood's risk team will send a short onboarding checklist to Durable and push the change to our subprocessor roster (this will be reflected in the next roster update).

For audit trail: request id MDOPS-4512 (HubSpot). DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/envelope/ABC-DEF-2027

Please see attached: permission_acknowledgement_signed.pdf (placeholder until we receive the signed copy).

Regards,
